canonical_question: Why is there a discrepancy between the reported compression yield strength of 929 MPa [ [2] ] and 1073 MPa [ [9] ], and what processing differences might explain this variation?

question_variants.question: Why is there a discrepancy between the reported compression yield strength of 929 MPa [ [2] ] and 1073 MPa [ [9] ], and what processing differences might explain this variation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text reports two different compression yield strength values (929 MPa and 1073 MPa) attributed to references [2] and [9] (Senkov et al.), but does not explain the discrepancy or detail the processing differences (e.g., annealing time, cooling rate) that might account for the variation.

answers.answer: The text notes a reported compression yield strength of 929 MPa [ [2] ] and 1073 MPa [ [9] ] for the Ta-Nb-Hf-Zr-Ti alloy. While it describes the general processing (vacuum arc melting, re-melting, HIP at 1200 °C, annealing at 1200 °C for 24 h), it does not provide the specific processing differences or explain the cause of the discrepancy between the two reported values.
answers.processing_state: HIP at 1200 °C, annealed at 1200 °C for 24 h
answers.measurement_outcome: Yield strength reported as 929 MPa and 1073 MPa.
answers.boundary_limitation: No explanation for the yield strength discrepancy provided.
evidence_spans: Among the various systems of alloying elements studied, the Ta 20 Nb 20 Hf 20 Zr 20 Ti 20 alloy seems to be attractive due to its reduced density of 9.94 g/cm 3 [ [2] , [3] ]

As reported by Senkov et al. [ [2] , [3] ], the process of producing the Ta 20 Nb 20 Hf 20 Zr 20 Ti 20 alloy consisted of vacuum arc melting followed by re-melting the material three times, five minutes each time, in order to achieve homogeneity. After that, the material underwent Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) at 1200 °C and 207 MPa for 1 h and finally underwent vacuum annealing at 1200 °C for 24 h.

According to Senkov et al. [ [2] , [3] , [7] , [8] ], after annealing at 1200 °C for 24 h the alloy was found to have a single-phase Body Centered Cubic (BCC) solid solution with a lattice parameter of 0.3404 nm, and its microstructure consisted of equiaxed, dendritic grains with an average size of 100–200 μm.
